criteria.criterion: NASA's DART mission changed Dimorphos' orbital period around Didymos by at least 73 seconds
required_elements: NASA defined success as an orbit period change for Dimorphos of 73 seconds or more
DART actually changed Dimorphos' orbit period around Didymos by at least 73 seconds
criteria.promise_scope: Actor: NASA. Intended object/beneficiary: Dimorphos' orbit around Didymos. Location: in space at the Dimorphos-Didymos asteroid system. Benefit/action: a successful DART outcome was defined as changing Dimorphos' orbital period by 73 seconds or more. Material condition: threshold is at least 73 seconds of change.
criteria.observed_scope: Actor: NASA/DART investigation team. Actual object affected: Dimorphos’ orbit around Didymos. Location: the Dimorphos-Didymos asteroid system in space. Actual action established: DART altered Dimorphos’ orbital period by 32 minutes, later settling at 33 minutes and 15 seconds shorter than before impact.
criteria.explanation: The original success criterion was NASA’s definition of a minimum orbit period change of 73 seconds or more for Dimorphos. Observed outcomes directly report that DART changed Dimorphos’ orbit around Didymos by 32 minutes, and later by 33 minutes and 15 seconds less than before impact. Those reported changes are far greater than 73 seconds, so the requested target was met. The later NASA statement that DART successfully altered Dimorphos’ orbit is consistent with those quantified results.

delivery_support.quote: Now, the investigation team has confirmed the spacecraft’s impact altered Dimorphos’ orbit around Didymos by 32 minutes, shortening the 11 hour and 55-minute orbit to 11 hours and 23 minutes.

Over the following weeks, the asteroid’s orbital period continued to shorten as Dimorphos lost more rocky material to space, finally settling at 11 hours, 22 minutes, and 3 seconds per orbit – 33 minutes and 15 seconds less time than before impact.

After further analysis, NASA confirmed that DART’s hypervelocity impact with Dimorphos successfully altered Dimorphos’ orbit around Didymos, marking humanity’s first time purposely changing the motion of a celestial object and the first demonstration of asteroid deflection technology.

NASA's DART mission changed Dimorphos' orbital period around Didymos by at least 73 seconds
Status: DELIVERED
The original success criterion was NASA’s definition of a minimum orbit period change of 73 seconds or more for Dimorphos. Observed outcomes directly report that DART changed Dimorphos’ orbit around Didymos by 32 minutes, and later by 33 minutes and 15 seconds less than before impact. Those reported changes are far greater than 73 seconds, so the requested target was met. The later NASA statement that DART successfully altered Dimorphos’ orbit is consistent with those quantified results.

Benefit/action: a successful DART outcome was defined as changing Dimorphos' orbital period by 73 seconds or more. Material condition: threshold is at least 73 seconds of change.
Observed scope: Actor: NASA/DART investigation team. Actual object affected: Dimorphos’ orbit around Didymos. Location: the Dimorphos-Didymos asteroid system in space. Supported delivery: NASA's DART mission changed Dimorphos' orbital period around Didymos by at least 73 seconds.
Promise evidence: c1
Delivery evidence: c2, c3, c4

Cited source excerpts (promise, delivery, or context as assessed above):
c1: “Before its encounter, NASA had defined a minimum successful orbit period change of Dimorphos as change of 73 seconds or more.”
https://www.nasa.gov/news-release/nasa-confirms-dart-mission-impact-changed-asteroids-motion-in-space/

c2: “Prior to DART’s impact, it took Dimorphos 11 hours and 55 minutes to orbit its larger parent asteroid, Didymos. Since DART’s intentional collision with Dimorphos on Sept. 26, astronomers have been using telescopes on Earth to measure how much that time has changed. Now, the investigation team has confirmed the spacecraft’s impact altered Dimorphos’ orbit around Didymos by 32 minutes, shortening the 11 hour and 55-minute orbit to 11 hours and 23 minutes. This measurement has a margin of uncertainty of approximately plus or minus 2 minutes.”
https://www.nasa.gov/news-release/nasa-confirms-dart-mission-impact-changed-asteroids-motion-in-space/

c3: “Over the following weeks, the asteroid’s orbital period continued to shorten as Dimorphos lost more rocky material to space, finally settling at 11 hours, 22 minutes, and 3 seconds per orbit – 33 minutes and 15 seconds less time than before impact. This calculation is accurate to within 1 1⁄2 seconds, Naidu said.”
https://www.nasa.gov/missions/dart/nasa-study-asteroids-orbit-shape-changed-after-dart-impact/?rand=772114

c4: “After further analysis, NASA confirmed that DART’s hypervelocity impact with Dimorphos successfully altered Dimorphos’ orbit around Didymos, marking humanity’s first time purposely changing the motion of a celestial object and the first demonstration of asteroid deflection technology.”
https://science.nasa.gov/planetary-defense-dart/
